references.notes: Figure 4.8 reproduces Wetzel and Schmidt’s excavation plan of the main temple and eastern annex. Figures 4.9–4.10 show the layers and sections at the courtyard and rooms 7 and 12. Figure 4.11 distinguishes attested exterior walls from the reconstructed subdivisions of the annex.

Figure 2 shows the principal excavation pit and the separate Etemenanki site. The reported Nebuchadnezzar-stamped building floors are at 29.8 and 29.9 m above sea level. This model places the represented floor at their midpoint.
The excavation volume records the north facade at 79.3 m and west facade at 85.8 m. The separate eastern annex projects beyond the principal temple at the south.
The site record describes the central sanctuary and distinguishes the excavated temple from the modern archaeological landscape.

limitations: The perimeter and main courtyard follow excavation controls. Reconstructed door elevations, roof heights and western cella geometry are interpretive. The internal arrangement of the eastern annex is provisional.
The excavated pit anchors the plan. The bearing derives from the printed north arrow. The ancient floor datum and terrain require an integrated dated view to confirm site fit.
Dated placement is pending. The reconstruction represents the sixth century BCE and the current viewing-date API accepts Common Era dates.
